findings.evidence: Lines 59-62 define `tensorCombine` solely using `TensorProduct.tensorTensorTensorComm` and `LinearMap.mul' R C`; Mathlib has `LinearMap.mul'` under `[NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring A] [Module R A] [SMulCommClass R A A] [IsScalarTower R A A]` (`mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Bilinear.lean:24-40`), while `Bialgebra` extends both `Algebra` and `Coalgebra` (`mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Basic.lean:57-58`).
findings.fix: Split the assumptions: state the combining map section under the assumptions needed by `LinearMap.mul'`, e.g. `[Semiring C] [Algebra R C]` (or the exact weaker `LinearMap.mul'` assumptions), and add `[Coalgebra R C]`/`[Comodule R C _]` only for `tensorCoact` and `tensorCoact_natural`.
findings.issue: `tensorCombine`, `tensorCombine_tmul_tmul`, and `tensorCombine_natural` inherit `[Bialgebra R C]`, but they only use the `R`-linear multiplication on `C`; no coalgebra structure or bialgebra compatibility appears in their statements or proofs.

summary: The new tensor-combine API is stated at the bialgebra level even though the construction and its naturality only use the multiplication as a linear map. This makes the public lemmas less reusable than the natural Mathlib-level assumptions.
